summary: Single-reviewer Phase-4 design critique (rubber-duck, opus-4.8). Core design confirmed sound: single chokepoint (build_hooks_for_config) verified, the None -> empty-program -> cmd.exe mechanism verified against registry.rs:80 + command_runner.rs:104-126, Strategy A correctly fixes BOTH git-bash and WSL cases, Strategy B rightly rejected, and both verify-only claims hold. Two must-fix findings (B1, B2) and four doc/robustness findings (N1-N4) were ALL adopted into the plan before finalization.

findings.title: shell.shell_type is a pub(crate) FIELD, not a method
findings.detail: The plan's predicate used shell.shell_type() which would not compile. core/src/shell.rs:11 declares `pub(crate) shell_type: ShellType`; the only method is name(). build_hooks_for_config is in codex-core (same crate) so it accesses the field directly.
findings.resolution: Plan updated: predicate uses field access `shell.shell_type`; the suggested shell_type() accessor was removed (no API widening).

findings.title: Naive truth-table test fails on ubuntu CI
findings.detail: invariant-check.yml runs `cargo test --workspace` on ubuntu AND windows. A predicate that is false on non-Windows makes assert!(...(bash)) fail on Linux.
findings.resolution: Plan updated: unit-test assertions are platform-gated (POSIX rows == cfg!(windows); PowerShell/Cmd always false). AC updated to require green on both platforms.

findings.title: Use cfg!(windows) in the fn body, not #[cfg] on the fn/import
findings.detail: Gating the fn or the ShellType import with #[cfg(windows)] leaves ShellType unused on the other platform and breaks the cross-platform build. cfg!(windows) is const-false on non-Windows but still type-checks the matches!.
findings.resolution: Plan updated to a single un-gated fn: `cfg!(windows) && matches!(shell.shell_type, ...)`.

findings.title: Regression test should not depend on node/bash being installed
findings.detail: A test resolving `node <backslash-path>` needs a real Windows node + bash path and is brittle. A cmd-only expansion `echo %OS%` -> assert stdout contains Windows_NT pins the interpreter switch with zero external dependency (bogus bash path is never invoked after the fix).
findings.resolution: Plan + stories + AC updated to the `echo %OS%` -> Windows_NT behavioral test shape (Windows-gated).

findings.title: Document post-fix interpreter-on-PATH constraint (WSL node)
findings.detail: After the fix a git-bash/WSL hook runs under cmd.exe and needs a Windows interpreter on PATH; a WSL-only node still won't run hooks (unsolvable without path translation; prior behavior was already broken).
findings.resolution: Added as a Risk bullet and required in the patch-surface §15 note.

findings.title: Document that a bare POSIX command now runs under cmd.exe
findings.detail: A hook authored with POSIX-only syntax in the bare `command` field, relying on a git-bash session shell, now runs under cmd.exe on Windows. Escape hatch = the `command_windows` field (discovery.rs:470). Net-positive (the prior path was already broken by mangling).
findings.resolution: Required in the patch-surface §15 note; the existing Risk bullet about bash-semantics hooks already references command_windows.

findings.title: Spaces in plugin-root path break cmd.exe token-splitting
findings.detail: An unquoted `node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/...` with a space-containing install root (C:\Users\John Doe\...) breaks under cmd.exe. This is pre-existing hooks.json authoring (bash would break too) and a property of the native default, not introduced by this fix.
findings.resolution: Out of scope; already flagged in plan Risk Areas + Out of Scope so it is not mistaken for a regression. No action in this plan.
